rows.Origin:
Bred by Reimer Kordes (1922-1997) (Germany, 1966).
Introduced in United Kingdom by Dickson Nurseries Ltd. / Dickson Roses as 'Peter Frankenfeld'.
Introduced in Australia by Treloar Roses in 1967 as 'Peter Frankenfeld'.
rows.Bloom: Rose-pink. Mild fragrance. Average diameter 4.25". Large, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Medium, spreading. Medium green, leathery foliage.

Height: 4' to 5' (120 to 150cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b and warmer. Can be used for beds and borders, cut flower or garden. Disease susceptibility: disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
